text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies.

The intense pruritus and new-onset 'red bumps' (papules) on the thigh, particularly in the context of recent close contact at a conference, are highly suggestive of a parasitic infestation. The distribution and severity of the itch, often worse at night, combined with the specific lesions, point toward this diagnosis over simple eczema or insect bites.
